name: Bahdanau Attention
introducedBy: Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio
introducedFor: RNN encoder-decoder machine translation
paperTitle: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
summary: The original attention mechanism: let a decoder look back at every encoder state and learn which ones matter for the current output word.
keyIdea: Scores each encoder state with a small feed-forward network instead of a fixed alignment, then takes a weighted sum.

name: Luong Attention
introducedBy: Luong, Pham & Manning
introducedFor: RNN-based neural machine translation
paperTitle: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
summary: A simpler, faster alternative to Bahdanau attention that scores alignment with a dot product or small bilinear term instead of a full feed-forward network.
keyIdea: Introduced global vs. local attention variants, and the dot-product scoring function that scaled dot-product attention later built on.

name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
introducedBy: Vaswani et al. (Google Brain / Google Research)
introducedFor: The original Transformer architecture
paperTitle: Attention Is All You Need
summary: The core operation behind virtually every modern LLM: compare a query to every key with a dot product, scale, softmax, then take a weighted sum of values.
keyIdea: softmax(QKᵀ / √dₖ)V — dividing by √dₖ keeps the dot products from growing too large and flattening the softmax gradient.

name: Multi-Head Attention
introducedBy: Vaswani et al. (Google Brain / Google Research)
introducedFor: The original Transformer architecture
paperTitle: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Runs several scaled dot-product attention operations in parallel, each with its own learned projections, so different heads can specialize in different relationships.
keyIdea: Split the model dimension across h independent heads, attend separately, then concatenate and project back — giving the model several 'representation subspaces' at once.

name: Self-Attention
introducedBy: Vaswani et al. (Google Brain / Google Research)
introducedFor: Letting a sequence attend to itself instead of a separate source sequence
paperTitle: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Queries, keys, and values all come from the same sequence, so every token can directly weigh every other token in one step — no recurrence needed.
keyIdea: Replacing recurrence with direct token-to-token comparison is what let Transformers parallelize training and capture long-range dependencies so much better than RNNs.

name: Cross-Attention
introducedBy: Vaswani et al. (Google Brain / Google Research)
introducedFor: Letting a decoder attend to a separate encoder's output
paperTitle: Attention Is All You Need
summary: Queries come from one sequence (e.g. the decoder) while keys and values come from another (e.g. the encoder) — the mechanism that lets translation and multimodal models fuse two inputs.
keyIdea: Generalizes attention to two different sequences instead of one, which is also how text-to-image and vision-language models fuse modalities today.

name: Causal (Masked) Self-Attention
introducedBy: Vaswani et al.; popularized for language modeling by Radford et al. (OpenAI)
introducedFor: Autoregressive, decoder-only language modeling (GPT)
paperTitle: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
summary: Self-attention with a triangular mask so each token can only see itself and earlier tokens — essential for models that generate text one token at a time.
keyIdea: Masking future positions with -∞ before softmax makes training on a whole sequence at once equivalent to next-token prediction, without leaking the answer.

name: Sparse Transformer
introducedBy: Child, Gray, Radford & Sutskever (OpenAI)
introducedFor: Modeling very long sequences (text, images, audio) affordably
paperTitle: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers
summary: Instead of attending to every previous token, each token attends to a structured subset (e.g. a local window plus a strided pattern) to cut cost on long inputs.
keyIdea: Factorizing full attention into a small number of sparse patterns whose union still lets information flow across the whole sequence in a few layers.

name: Multi-Query Attention
introducedBy: Noam Shazeer (Google)
introducedFor: Faster autoregressive decoding by shrinking the KV cache
paperTitle: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
summary: All query heads share a single key/value head instead of each having its own — a big memory win at some cost to quality.
keyIdea: The real bottleneck in autoregressive decoding is memory bandwidth for re-reading the KV cache, not compute — so shrinking K/V storage speeds up generation a lot.

name: Reformer (LSH Attention)
introducedBy: Kitaev, Kaiser & Levskaya (Google)
introducedFor: Making very long-context Transformers memory-efficient
paperTitle: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer
summary: Uses locality-sensitive hashing to bucket similar queries and keys together, so each token only attends within its bucket instead of the whole sequence.
keyIdea: Tokens likely to have high attention scores tend to hash to the same bucket, so LSH turns full attention into an approximate nearest-neighbor search.

name: Longformer Attention
introducedBy: Beltagy, Peters & Cohan (Allen Institute for AI)
introducedFor: Long-document NLP tasks (summarization, QA)
paperTitle: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
summary: Combines a local sliding window (every token attends to nearby tokens) with a few 'global' tokens that attend to and are attended by everything.
keyIdea: Local context covers most linguistic structure cheaply, while a handful of global tokens (like [CLS]) still let information travel across the whole document.

name: BigBird Attention
introducedBy: Zaheer et al. (Google Research)
introducedFor: Longer sequences for NLP and genomics
paperTitle: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences
summary: Blends random attention, a local window, and global tokens — proven to still be a universal sequence approximator despite being sparse.
keyIdea: Random attention edges act like random graph shortcuts, keeping the effective 'distance' between any two tokens small even though most pairs never attend directly.

name: Linformer
introducedBy: Wang, Li, Khabsa, Fang & Ma (Facebook AI)
introducedFor: Linear-time self-attention
paperTitle: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
summary: Projects the keys and values down to a fixed, smaller size before attending, based on the observation that attention matrices are often approximately low-rank.
keyIdea: If attention is approximately low-rank, you can compress the sequence dimension of K and V with a learned linear projection with little accuracy loss.

name: Performer
introducedBy: Choromanski et al. (Google)
introducedFor: Unbiased, linear-time approximation of softmax attention
paperTitle: Rethinking Attention with Performers
summary: Approximates the softmax attention kernel using random feature maps, avoiding ever materializing the full n×n attention matrix.
keyIdea: FAVOR+ (Fast Attention Via positive Orthogonal Random features) gives a provably unbiased estimate of regular softmax attention while running in linear time.

name: FlashAttention
introducedBy: Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra & Ré (Stanford)
introducedFor: Exact attention without the memory/speed penalty of materializing the full attention matrix
paperTitle: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
summary: Not a new attention pattern — an IO-aware algorithm that computes the exact same attention output while avoiding slow reads/writes to GPU high-bandwidth memory.
keyIdea: Tiles the computation into blocks that fit in fast on-chip SRAM, using online softmax so the full n×n score matrix never has to be written to HBM.
usedIn: Superseded by FlashAttention-2/3/4 in current training stacks

name: FlashAttention-2
introducedBy: Tri Dao (Princeton / Together AI)
introducedFor: Better GPU parallelism and work partitioning than FlashAttention
paperTitle: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
summary: Reworks FlashAttention's parallelization to cut non-matmul operations and better use GPU warps, roughly doubling throughput.
keyIdea: Better work partitioning across thread blocks and warps pushes GPU utilization much closer to what optimized matrix multiplication achieves.
usedIn: Standard on Ampere-class and older GPUs (A100 and earlier) across most training/inference stacks

name: FlashAttention-3
introducedBy: Shah, Bikshandi, Zhang, Thakkar, Ramani & Dao (Colfax Research, Meta, NVIDIA, Together AI, Princeton)
introducedFor: Exploiting Hopper-generation GPU features (H100) that FlashAttention-2 left on the table
paperTitle: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
summary: Overlaps computation and data movement using Hopper's asynchronous Tensor Cores, and adds a low-precision (FP8) mode.
keyIdea: Warp-specialization plus interleaving matmul and softmax steps pushed H100 utilization from ~35% to ~75% of theoretical peak.

name: FlashAttention-4
introducedBy: Tri Dao and collaborators (Princeton, Together AI, Meta, NVIDIA, Colfax Research)
introducedFor: Rearchitecting attention for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, where non-matmul units became the new bottleneck
paperTitle: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
summary: A ground-up redesign for Blackwell GPUs (B200/B300) that software-emulates exponentials on FMA units and skips unnecessary softmax rescaling to work around shifted hardware bottlenecks.
keyIdea: As matmul throughput on Blackwell outpaced shared-memory bandwidth and exponential units, FA4 co-designs the algorithm around those new bottlenecks instead of the old ones — reaching attention speeds close to raw matmul.

name: Grouped-Query Attention
introducedBy: Ainslie, Lee-Thorp, de Jong, Zemlyanskiy, Lebrón & Sanghai (Google Research)
introducedFor: Interpolating between MHA's quality and MQA's speed
paperTitle: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
summary: Query heads are split into groups, and each group shares one key/value head — g=1 recovers MQA, g=h recovers full MHA.
keyIdea: A tunable dial between MQA's efficiency and MHA's quality; existing MHA checkpoints can be 'uptrained' into GQA with a small fraction of extra training.
usedIn: the de facto default for most current open-weight models

name: Sliding Window Attention
introducedBy: Popularized in production by Mistral AI
introducedFor: Bounding attention cost per token regardless of total context length
paperTitle: Mistral 7B
summary: Each token only attends to the most recent w tokens instead of the entire sequence, capping per-token attention cost at a fixed window size.
keyIdea: Stacked across layers, a fixed window still lets information propagate across a much larger effective receptive field, similar in spirit to convolutional receptive fields.

name: Attention Sinks (StreamingLLM)
introducedBy: Xiao, Tian, Chen, Han & Lewis (MIT, Meta AI, Carnegie Mellon)
introducedFor: Letting sliding-window LLMs handle effectively infinite streaming text without fine-tuning
paperTitle: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
summary: Discovered that models dump disproportionate attention onto the very first few tokens as a stabilizing 'sink' — keeping just those tokens plus a sliding window recovers full-attention-quality streaming.
keyIdea: Softmax always has to sum to 1, so when nothing is relevant the model needs somewhere to dump the leftover probability mass — the first tokens become that dumping ground.

name: Ring Attention
introducedBy: Liu, Zaharia & Abbeel (UC Berkeley)
introducedFor: Training/inference on near-infinite context by distributing sequences across many devices
paperTitle: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
summary: Splits a very long sequence into blocks across a ring of devices, overlapping the communication of key/value blocks with the attention computation itself.
keyIdea: Because the communication is fully hidden behind computation, effective context length scales with the number of devices, with no extra communication overhead.

name: Multi-Head Latent Attention
introducedBy: DeepSeek-AI
introducedFor: Shrinking the KV cache far more aggressively than GQA without MQA's quality loss
paperTitle: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
summary: Compresses keys and values into a small shared latent vector (like a learned low-rank projection) instead of storing separate K/V per head or group.
keyIdea: Caching a compressed latent representation — and reconstructing per-head K/V from it on the fly — gets GQA-or-better quality at closer to MQA-level cache size.

name: Differential Attention
introducedBy: Ye, Dong, Xia, Sun, Zhu, Huang & Wei (Microsoft Research, Tsinghua University)
introducedFor: Reducing 'attention noise' — wasted attention mass on irrelevant context
paperTitle: Differential Transformer
complexity: O(n²), roughly 2× the projections of standard attention
summary: Computes attention as the difference between two separate softmax attention maps, so common-mode noise cancels out and only genuine signal remains.
keyIdea: Two attention maps, subtracted with a learned weight λ, naturally suppress the noisy attention that plain softmax struggles to fully zero out, sharpening focus on truly relevant tokens.
usedIn: Research models; cited as a building block in several 2025 efficient-attention follow-ups

name: Native Sparse Attention
introducedBy: Yuan, Gao, Dai et al. (DeepSeek-AI, Peking University)
introducedFor: Hardware-aligned sparse attention that can be trained end-to-end, not just applied at inference
paperTitle: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
summary: Combines three parallel branches — compressed coarse attention, selected important blocks, and a local sliding window — tuned to run efficiently on real GPU hardware.
keyIdea: Unlike most sparse-attention methods that are bolted on after pretraining, NSA is designed to be trained from scratch, matching or beating full attention quality at a fraction of the cost on 64K+ token sequences.
usedIn: DeepSeek research models; referenced as related work in DeepSeek-V3.2
